_doc: Uncovered units (statements never executed + branches taken in only one direction + lines excluded by a `# pragma: no cover`) per hard-rule surface, as measured by the FULL suite under `coverage run` FROM EMPTY STORES — a freshly migrated and seeded database AND a Redis holding nothing — which is what CI provisions and what `make coverage-ratchet-accept` requires. What those two hold changes which branches execute, so this is enforced rather than remembered: the gate REFUSES to score, and refuses to write this file, from a run that started with leftover data, or that was filtered, failing, or missing a service. The gate is an EQUALITY: more is a regression, less is an improvement that must be locked in here. NEVER hand-edit a number here to quieten a red gate — that is how both of this file's fictional regressions were committed, and the edit lands on the next person's PR. That is not a slogan: `voice-runtime-ack` was edited twice for a divergence that was never a coverage change at all. webhook_routes.py:182 (the >500ms ack alert) fired only when the machine was slow, so a busy runner covered it and an idle laptop did not, and this file's EQUALITY went red in both directions across nine commits — once as an unlocked improvement at 22, then eight times as a phantom regression at 24. It is fixed where it belonged, in a test that drives the slow path by lowering the threshold instead of hoping the runner is busy, so every machine now measures 22. There is no known speed-dependent branch left and NO area for which CI's number is the authority; a future one gets the same treatment, not an edit here. See scripts/check_coverage_ratchet.py's docstring for that account and for why this is a count per area, not a percentage.
